data.one_liner: Flexible and lightweight dependency injection library for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Cherrypick provides a system for registering, scoping, and resolving dependencies using modular bindings and hierarchical scopes. It supports singletons, lazy providers, asynchronous factories, and automatic resource cleanup for disposable dependencies.
use_when: You want hierarchical scopes and modular composition in your dependency injection setup.
You need automatic resource cleanup via the Disposable interface.
You want support for both manual configuration and annotation-based code generation.
avoid_when: You prefer a heavily runtime-reflected DI container without module definitions.
Your project uses an entirely different state management or service locator solution like get_it and you don't want to migrate.
strengths: Supports hierarchical subscopes and named instances.
Automatic resource cleanup for Disposable dependencies.
Both manual bindings and annotation-based code generation are supported.
weaknesses: Potential misuse of bindings inside modules (e.g., resolving types via toInstance during registration can cause errors).
Requires careful lifecycle management of scopes and singletons.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding cherrypick to pubspec.yaml, and optionally cherrypick_annotations and cherrypick_generator with build_runner if using code generation.

alternatives.name: get_it
alternatives.why_pick_it: A widely adopted, straightforward service locator for Dart and Flutter that doesn't require modules or code generation.

alternatives.name: injectable
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides extensive annotation-based code generation built on top of get_it for automatic dependency injection wiring.
